rounds.text: Despite reported profits, SPML Infra Ltd carries severe fundamental and technical risks that undermine its valuation. Most critically, the company suffers from a complete disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash generation, evidenced by a cash conversion of -1.51x and a staggering negative operating cash flow of Rs -113 Cr alongside a negative free cash flow of Rs -179 Cr in March 2026 [E28, E30]. Furthermore, long-term top-line expansion remains stagnant with a 10-year compounded sales growth of -8% and a poor 5-year sales growth of 4.93%, while profitability metrics are subpar with a 10-year median return on equity of just 4% and a 3-year average of 6.31% [E8, E57, E59]. Market sentiment and technical health are deeply depressed, with the stock sitting near its 52-week low at 24% of its range, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and suffering a lagging relative-strength rating of 22 against the Nifty 500 [E5, E44, E45]. Compounding these concerns, the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield, exhibits low tax rates, and faces flags regarding potential interest cost capitalization alongside a recent quarterly drop in promoter holdings [E4, E56, E58, E60]. Conceded: the company displays strong short-term profit growth with a 5-year CAGR of 55.7%, positive institutional money flow, and a discounted cash flow valuation pointing to a high margin of safety [E13, E38, E39, E54].
